title: Scientists Put Caterpillars in an Ultraquiet Chamber to Learn How They Hear Without Ears
summary: The research could do more than help unlock the mystery of caterpillar hearing. It could also help make microphones better.
llm_summary: Scientists have placed caterpillars in an ultra‑quiet chamber and measured the tiny vibrations that travel through their bodies, revealing how these earless insects detect sound. By decoding this natural “mechanical microphone,” the work not only solves a long‑standing biological mystery but also offers fresh design cues for ultra‑sensitive, low‑noise microphones and other acoustic sensors.
